title: cohort-harmonise: dictionary-first harmonisation and claim auditing across youth-development cohorts

creators.name: Wichstrom, Lars
creators.affiliation: Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Trondheim, Norway

description:
A dictionary-first harmonisation tool for aligning constructs across five longitudinal youth-development cohorts — LSAC (Growing Up in Australia), ABCD, TESS (Trondheim Early Secure Study), Ten to Men and LSIC (Footprints in Time) — using variable-level metadata only, with no access to participant data and no redistribution of dictionary files.

Cohorts and target constructs are configuration rather than code, so the tool generalises to constructs and cohorts beyond the anxiety application it was built for. Four adapters cover the dictionary shapes encountered, including inventories built from published documentation for cohorts with no custodian codebook; every row records the tier of evidence it rests on, distinguishing a custodian dictionary from a published cohort profile from a reconstruction assembled from methods sections.

Outputs: a construct coverage matrix over primary waves; a register of constructs declared non-harmonisable, each with a mandatory stated reason and empirical confirmation of absence; an assessment, for every cohort pair, of whether genuine common items exist to anchor a multi-group latent model or whether the inference must be harmonised instead of the scale; a check that the cohorts holding a construct agree on who reported it; and an audit of published methodological claims against the cohorts' own dictionaries.

Verdicts are evidence-tier aware. A cohort read from a custodian dictionary can contradict a claim; a cohort inventoried from publications can only fail to confirm one, and is reported as unverifiable rather than false. A declared absence is confirmed only for cohorts where a dictionary exists to confirm it in.

Data governance is enforced in code rather than described in prose: a governed cohort is excluded unless explicitly included, its culturally grounded wellbeing indicators cannot be mapped as standing in for a diagnostic construct, and a non-harmonisable declaration without a stated reason raises an error. Provenance records a SHA-256 over every dictionary read, so a third party can confirm they ran against the same releases without those files being redistributed.
notes: No participant data is read, produced or redistributed by this software: it operates on variable-level metadata only, and no cohort dictionary file is included in this archive. Reproducing the reports requires obtaining each dictionary from its custodian under that study's own terms; docs/data_sources.md lists the expected paths and sources, and outputs/provenance.json records a SHA-256 over each file read so a third party can confirm they ran against the same releases. One cohort is governed under the CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance and the Maiam nayri Wingara Indigenous Data Sovereignty Principles; it is excluded from the published outputs unless sign-off is documented.
